[DEV-ARCH-2026]
Title: Current Designer extension development architecture
Date: 2026-06-18

For ordinary Designer extension work, run the Vite client locally and point it at the existing hosted API on wfdev.io. The hosted environment continues to own the database, OAuth exchange, provider credentials, and callback handling. This keeps the local loop fast without reproducing production infrastructure. A full local backend is reserved for work that changes server behavior, database migrations, or the OAuth callback implementation.

[TEAM-LOOP-2026]
Title: Team workflow for ordinary extension changes
Date: 2026-07-02

The supported daily loop is pnpm dev for the local Vite client with environment values targeting the hosted development API. Developers use the hosted development database and existing OAuth installation. They do not run database containers or replay migrations for UI-only work. If a task changes an API contract, authentication behavior, persistence, or provider callback behavior, plan the appropriate server-side environment separately.

[OAUTH-BOUNDARY-2026]
Title: OAuth callback and secret ownership
Date: 2026-05-09

The registered provider callback is the HTTPS wfdev.io callback. The local Vite client may begin authorization through the hosted API, but the client secret and token exchange stay on the hosted server. Frontend-only development does not require a local callback or tunnel. A tunnel is needed only when deliberately testing a changed callback handler that must receive provider traffic on a developer machine.

Title: Designer extension security review
Date: 2026-04-27

Provider client secrets, refresh tokens, and database credentials must never be placed in Vite environment variables or browser code. The browser receives only public configuration and calls the hosted API. Local convenience does not justify moving confidential credentials across the server boundary.

[MIGRATION-TESTING-2026]
Title: Database migration testing procedure
Date: 2026-03-14

When a task changes the database schema, create an isolated database and run forward and rollback migrations before deploying to the hosted development environment. This procedure is specific to persistence changes. It does not require every frontend contributor to run a local database.

[FULL-LOCAL-SETUP-2024]
Title: Legacy full-local setup guide
Date: 2024-01-11

This archived guide predates wfdev.io. It runs the client, API, Postgres database, and OAuth callback locally, then exposes the callback through a tunnel. The document was written when no shared hosted development backend existed. It is retained for historical migrations and should not be treated as the current daily workflow.

item.text:
Use a split setup: run only the Vite client locally with `pnpm dev`, configured to call the development API on `wfdev.io`. Keep the API, OAuth flow, credentials, and database hosted. That is the current supported daily workflow and gives frontend work a fast loop without rebuilding production infrastructure locally. [DEV-ARCH-2026] [TEAM-LOOP-2026]

**OAuth and secrets**

Start authorization through the hosted API and keep the registered HTTPS callback on `wfdev.io`. The hosted server must perform the token exchange and hold provider secrets, refresh tokens, and database credentials. Vite variables and browser code should contain public configuration only. [OAUTH-BOUNDARY-2026] [SECURITY-REVIEW-2026]

**Database**

Use the hosted development database for ordinary extension work. Don't run Postgres containers or replay migrations for UI changes. For a schema change, create an isolated database and test both forward and rollback migrations before updating the hosted development environment. [TEAM-LOOP-2026] [MIGRATION-TESTING-2026]

**Tunnel**

No tunnel is needed for the normal workflow because provider traffic goes to the existing `wfdev.io` callback. Use one only when testing a changed callback handler that must receive provider requests on your machine. [OAUTH-BOUNDARY-2026]

The 2024 full local guide is stale because it predates the shared `wfdev.io` backend. Its local API, database, callback, and tunnel setup is historical guidance, not the default architecture. [FULL-LOCAL-SETUP-2024]

A broader local environment is justified when the task changes server behavior, an API contract, authentication, persistence, or the provider callback. For ordinary client work, keep the production shaped pieces hosted. [DEV-ARCH-2026] [TEAM-LOOP-2026]
